## The North Flank Collapse and the Blast at Mount St. Helens

In the two months before May 18, 1980, Mount St. Helens experienced earthquakes and small explosions. On May 18, its steep north flank collapsed in a landslide, triggering a blast that traveled nearly horizontally. A powerful vertical eruption followed, distinct from the blast.

The blast developed into a gravity-driven flow of hot material. It felled millions of trees, stripped bark and branches, and scraped away soil in places.
